slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you
sound more confident
when you talk
Speak a little slower than feels natural. Nerves make you rush. Slowing down gives your words weight and makes you sound like someone who expects to be heard.
Use pauses on purpose. Stop for a second before your main point. Silence builds attention, and confident speakers are never afraid of a short pause.
Lower your volume, don't raise it. When you want attention, speak softer, not louder. People lean in, and calm speech always sounds more sure than shouting.
Finish your sentences. Don't trail off with "and stuff" or "you know." Ending a sentence clearly tells people you meant every single word of it, and they listen better.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Knowing what you're talking about is the quickest way to sound confident about it.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Knowing your topic is the fastest way to sound confident.

slides.texte_overlay: Replace "I think maybe" with "I'd suggest." Small word changes make a big difference. Clear, direct phrases sound confident without sounding arrogant.
Record yourself once a week. A voice note of you telling a story. Listen back, notice your habits, and you'll improve faster than with any book or course.
